1: After Alexander the Great, the Greek king Antiochus Epiphanes plunders the Temple, bans the Jewish law and sets up a pagan altar. Many give in; many choose death.
A culture demands that God's people abandon their faith.
2: The old priest Mattathias refuses to offer pagan sacrifice and flees to the hills with his five sons. Dying, he tells them to give their lives for the covenant.
Resistance starts with one family saying no.
3: Judas, "the Hammer", takes command and wins his first battles against much larger forces.
"Victory does not depend on numbers; strength comes from heaven."
4: Judas defeats two more armies, cleanses the Temple and relights its lamps. The feast of Dedication is established.
This is the origin of Hanukkah, which Jesus kept.
5: Judas and his brothers fight to rescue Jews under attack in Galilee and Gilead.
Others who fight for their own glory are defeated.
6: Antiochus dies admitting the evil he did in Jerusalem. Eleazar dies killing a war elephant.
7: A new king sends the general Nicanor, who threatens the Temple. Judas defeats him.
8: Judas hears of Rome's power and makes an alliance.
9: Judas dies in battle against overwhelming odds. His brother Jonathan takes his place.
"How is the mighty fallen, the saviour of Israel!"
10: Rival kings compete for Jonathan's support, and he becomes high priest.
11: Kings rise and fall, and Jonathan negotiates among them.
Loyalty among these rulers is short-lived.
12: Jonathan renews ties with Rome and Sparta, then is tricked and seized by Trypho.
13: Simon, the last brother, takes command. Jonathan is killed. "The yoke of the Gentiles was removed from Israel."
14: The land has peace. The people record Simon's deeds on bronze tablets.
A portrait of peace under a good ruler.
15: King Antiochus VII first confirms Simon's rights, then turns on him.
Promises of the powerful shift with their interests.
16: Simon's sons defeat the enemy. Simon is killed at a banquet by his own son-in-law. His son John takes over.
The whole first generation gave their lives.
